Getting a response at least, but no luck getting nodes wierd let me run prysm with v5.1 using a v5.1 bootnode somehow the curve name of the priv key used in rumor is an empty string, and it fails then when signing which library are you using for secp256k1? libp2p crypto, which uses btcsuite: `privk, _ := btcec.PrivKeyFromBytes(btcec.S256(), data)` instead of the `.S256()` in geth yeah the go-ethereum library expects its own `crypto.S256()`, otherwise it won't work Yea, I read that piece of the code, comparing the curve instance But why can't it just use it? It's still the same crypto Making it compatible would be nice Will implement a work-around for now, serializing/deserializing into geth priv key, before handing it to discv5 Or maybe I can just overwrite the `.Curve`, feels hacky though I'm not sure how to make it work best. The go-ethereum `crypto.Sign` always uses its own curve implementation anyway. I need this check because I want to add support for ed25519 soon, and it has a different API for signing. hmm, maybe I could add a fallback using `ecdsa.Sign` there but not sure if it will work, and I don't have a good way to test this, it would never be used except in rumor Did the `.Curve` thing so it makes it into the `makeIDSignature` switch statement there. But now seeing `invalid ephemeral pubkey" in catdog logs any more specific message there? Prysm also uses libp2p crypto. Not sure how they deserialize their priv keys, with which type system etc. ``` TRACE[10-16|10:26:50.463] [v5.1] << UNKNOWN/v5 id=1f968f4fb49b1d3f addr=80.110.77.85:20072 TRACE[10-16|10:26:50.463] [v5.1] >> WHOAREYOU/v5 id=1f968f4fb49b1d3f addr=80.110.77.85:20072 DEBUG[10-16|10:26:50.665] [v5.1] Bad discv5 packet id=1f968f4fb49b1d3f addr=80.110.77.85:20072 err="invalid ephemeral pubkey" ``` No, this is all I get on the receiving end of the ping BTW libsecp256k1 is much faster, and is used for all the decoding/verification unless they explicitly build with nocgo Yeah we get the same error too Will keep that in mind, thanks. Just concerned about compatibility here though will have to shift it around a bit, shouldn't be too difficult though ``` var priv crypto.PrivKey priv, err = crypto.UnmarshalSecp256k1PrivateKey(privKeyBytes) if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse private key, invalid private key (Secp256k1): %v", err) } key := (priv).(*crypto.Secp256k1PrivateKey) key.Curve = gcrypto.S256() ``` Is my priv key loading code now. Libp2p, but with geth params override, so discv5 is happy. Ugly probably should just use geth directly, then cast that to libp2p crypto, but don't think it matters. It's just that `.Curve` + two big numbers (and yes, it's on curve and everything) Why can't you use `crypto.ToECDSA(privKeyBytes)` instead? Will do that. This was the libp2p way If you keep the private key as bytes, you can just unmarshal it differently for the different uses. That feels worse tbh hmm, maybe style prefs getting in the way there I mean, I could ask the same question: does libp2p accept the keys unmarshaled using our library? probably not! So it's like, each system wants the key treated with its own set of libraries But I agree it's annoying. Everything will get easier with ed25519 because its in the stdlib I mean that there already is a `Curve/X/Y` common ground and types. It's just a matter of recognizing the crypto, whoever provided the params and numbers but you can't recognize it based on the numbers alone, they're only meaningful if you know which curve they're on Anyway, still getting the same ephemeral key error with .ToECDSA, it's not the priv key that's wrong. yes I'm investigating this There's the `Curve.Params().Name`, but that isn't filled properly by every library either. yes Oh I think I got it <@!203220829473996800> do you know which implementation is sending this ping? The ephemeral pubkey again uses some switch statement But other end is not updated yet, still not recognizing the curve params So I need to copy that hack to the other end, and it should work... It's the v5wire `DecodePubkey` which has the same switch logic yes, but that should be fixed as well since your private key now has the right curve instance I hit the first error on the sending side. Need to fix remote catdog instance, which uses libp2p priv key parsing util Catdog is updated and can respond to v5.1 pings now Hmm, debugging catdog now, seeing if table is filled and I can get v5.0 records. It appears like some buckets are completely full, and others completely empty, that's weird
